coverage: Pre-market, Tue Nov 10. Latest verified closes are from Fri Nov 6
moodReason: The AI and chip selloff on Thu Nov 5 was the sharpest US drop since April 2025, and the Nasdaq is nearly 12% below its Oct 6 record. Strong October payrolls have pushed traders toward a December rate hike, which keeps pressure on richly valued tech.

stories.headline: AI and chip stocks suffer the worst sell-off since April 2025 on Thu Nov 5
stories.what: The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52%, the S&P 500 dropped about 4.4% to 7,353.73 and the Dow lost about 3.44%, or more than 1,800 points. Reuters estimated about $3 trillion of value was wiped from S&P 500 companies. The Nasdaq is now nearly 12% below its Oct 6 record.
stories.why: AI and chip companies carry large weights in the major indexes, so doubts about data center spending and tighter AI rules hit the whole market. Reports tie the fear to the midterm results, with Democrats winning control of both chambers of Congress.

stories.headline: October payrolls beat forecasts with 165,000 jobs and unemployment at 4.1%
stories.what: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported 165,000 new jobs in October, against forecasts of roughly 59,000 to 65,000. The unemployment rate fell 0.1 point to 4.1%, hourly wages rose 3.1% from a year earlier, and September was revised up to 60,000.
stories.why: A strong labor market makes the Fed less likely to cut and more open to another hike. That lifts yields and the dollar, and it weighs on long-duration tech stocks.

stories.headline: Traders price a high chance of a December Fed rate hike
stories.what: The Fed funds target range is 3.75% to 4.00%. Market pricing for a rate increase at the Dec 8 to 9 meeting is roughly 70% to 80%, though sources differ on the exact odds.
stories.why: Higher policy rates raise borrowing costs across the economy and lift the discount rate applied to future earnings, which hurts valuations most in growth stocks.

stories.headline: Oil swings on US strikes in Iran and later talk hopes
stories.what: US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island on Nov 3 pushed Brent to about $106.60 a barrel. Brent had eased to $97.94 by Fri Nov 6, and WTI was about $90.54.
stories.why: Oil near $90 to $100 keeps inflation expectations high, which supports the case for tighter policy. Any renewed flare-up in the Middle East could push prices back up quickly.

stories.headline: Small Friday rebound for stocks, led by Nasdaq and the Russell 2000
stories.what: On Fri Nov 6 the S&P 500 rose 0.32% to 7,376.86 and the Nasdaq gained 1.09% to 24,579.42. The Russell 2000 rose 0.87% to 2,753.65, while the Dow slipped 0.46%.
stories.why: The bounce shows dip buyers are active, but it recovered only a small part of Thursday's losses. Whether it holds depends on how the CPI report and the AI trade develop this week.

stories.headline: Marvell agrees to buy Lumentum in a $115 billion all-stock deal
stories.what: Marvell Technology agreed on Nov 2 to acquire optical components maker Lumentum in an all-stock transaction valued at $115 billion including debt.
stories.why: The deal consolidates suppliers of the optical links used in AI data centers, a segment that has been under pressure from the AI sell-off. Investors will look for how the combined company handles the sector's cyclical risks.

stories.headline: Earnings this week include CoreWeave, Cisco and Applied Materials
stories.what: CoreWeave reports after the close on Tue Nov 10, with its call at 5:00pm ET. Nebius reports before the open on Thu Nov 12, and Cisco and Applied Materials report after the close that day.
stories.why: CoreWeave, Nebius and the chip equipment makers give direct reads on AI data center spending, the same fear behind Thursday's sell-off. Their guidance could confirm or ease that worry.

bottomLine: US stocks are in a fragile spot after the sharpest AI-led sell-off since April 2025 and a Friday bounce that recovered only a small part of it. Strong October payrolls and a hawkish Fed tone have pushed the odds of a December hike to around 70% to 80%, while the 10-year yield sits near 4.86%. Today's CPI print and the AI-linked earnings this week will show whether the selling was a reset or the start of a deeper correction.
